title: Statement of the 3rd International Exercise-Associated Hyponatremia Consensus Development Conference, Carlsbad, California, 2015
claims: The primary aetiology and pathophysiological mechanism underlying exercise-associated hyponatremia and all known fatalities is overconsumption of hypotonic fluids relative to exchangeable sodium, likely combined with non-osmotic AVP secretion (Grade 1A).

Sodium supplementation can attenuate the fall in serum sodium when fluid intake approximates sweat losses, but cannot prevent exercise-associated hyponatremia when there is persistent excessive fluid intake causing fluid overload (Grade 1C).
All sports drinks are hypotonic to plasma, typically around 10-38 mmol/L sodium versus about 140 mmol/L serum; the dilution from excess volume overwhelms any protective effect of the beverage sodium.

Thirst should provide an adequate stimulus for preventing excess dehydration and markedly reduce the risk of hyponatremia; prevention targets drinking behavior, and excessive fluid beyond thirst is not a remedy for fatigue, collapse, cramping or exertional heat stroke.

Risk factors for EAH include overdrinking water, sports drinks or other hypotonic beverages, weight gain during exercise, exercise duration over 4 hours, event inexperience, slow performance pace, high or low body mass index, and readily available fluids.

claimVerification.note: Summary statement：“The primary aetiology and pathophysiological mechanism underlying EAH—and all known fatalities—is the overconsumption of hypotonic fluids relative to exchangeable sodium likely in combination with non-osmotic AVP secretion (Grade 1A).”

Summary statement：“Sodium supplementation is a strategy for attenuating sodium concentration reductions that can develop when fluid intakes approximate sweat losses during prolonged exercise but cannot prevent EAH in the setting of a persistent excessive fluid intake that produces fluid overload (Grade 1C).”

原文：“All sports beverages are hypotonic to plasma (typical sodium content in sports drinks are approximately 10–38 mmol/L)”；“all sports drinks have a significantly lower [Na+] (…–38 mmol/L) than serum (~140 mmol/L). The dilutional effect of volume excess overwhelms any positive effect of sodium”。

Role of thirst：“Thirst should provide adequate stimulus for preventing excess dehydration and markedly reduce the risk of developing EAH in all sports.”；Prevention：“Excessive fluid replacement beyond thirst … is not a panacea for all instances of fatigue, collapse, muscle cramping or exertional heat stroke.”

Box 2 Risk factors：Overdrinking water/sports drinks/hypotonic beverages、Weight gain during exercise、Exercise duration >4 h、Event inexperience or inadequate training、Slow running or performance pace、High or low body mass index、Readily available fluids。
